title.bn: goto দিয়ে নির্দিষ্ট স্থানে যাওয়া ও রিসোর্স ছাড়া

summary.en: goto targets a label in the same function.
summary.bn: goto-এর লাফ বোঝো, অপ্রয়োজনীয় লাফ এড়াও এবং এক জায়গায় resource cleanup করতে শেখো।

notes: goto and function-scope labels exist in C89. C99 added VLA-related jump restrictions. In C17, a label must precede a statement; put a null statement after a label if a declaration must follow. C23 relaxes some label-placement rules.

examples.title: A forward exit label
examples.explanationHtml: The false readiness flag causes a forward jump to finished. Work is skipped, and End prints. An if-else would express this tiny choice more directly; the example isolates the meaning of the transfer.

examples.title: A status reaches one reporting point
examples.explanationHtml: The condition does not jump because valid is one. Accepted prints, and ordinary fall-through reaches report. A label is not a barrier; normal execution can reach it just as a jump can.

examples.title: Release two possible allocations
examples.explanationHtml:
Successful allocations hold twelve and eight, producing total twenty. Both are then freed through cleanup. Either allocation failure instead reaches the same release section with status one. NULL initialization makes missing-resource cleanup safe.

The program never dereferences an allocation that failed.

practice.title: Skip one optional line
practice.statementHtml: Read ready 0 or 1. After the prompt Input: , print Work only for 1, then End on either path. Use a forward finished label.
hints: Place the shared final message at the target.

practice.title: One report point
practice.statementHtml: Read code 0 to 9. After the prompt Input: , print Valid when code is 3, otherwise skip that line. Then print Done on both paths using a report label.
hints: The label is also reached by fall-through.

practice.title: A reported failure flag
practice.statementHtml: Read valid 0 or 1. After the prompt Input: , print Accepted only for 1, then Status=0 for 1 or Status=1 for 0, each on its own line. Use a common report label.

practice.title: Simulate two acquired resources
practice.statementHtml: Read fail_stage 0, 1 or 2. After the prompt Input: , set acquired=1 after stage one succeeds and acquired=2 after stage two succeeds. Stage 1 or 2 fails when named by input; jump to cleanup then. Print Work only when neither fails. Always print Released=N with the number acquired, then newline.
hints: This model exposes every partial-ownership path without relying on allocation failure.

quiz.prompt: Where must a goto target label belong?
quiz.explanation: The jump cannot transfer between functions.

quiz.prompt: Can ordinary execution reach a label without goto?
quiz.explanation: Labels mark statements and do not block fall-through.

quiz.prompt: When is a cleanup goto useful?
options: Several failure paths share resource releases
quiz.explanation: One release section can handle partial ownership consistently.

quiz.prompt: What should a resource pointer contain before acquisition?
quiz.explanation: free(NULL) is safe on missing-resource paths.

quiz.prompt: Does a cleanup label run automatically before every return?
quiz.explanation: Control must actually reach the cleanup section.

options: A later read may use a value never assigned
Goto initializes every local to zero
quiz.explanation: Skipping initialization can invalidate the data flow.

quiz.prompt: What is usually clearer for ordinary repetition?
quiz.explanation: A loop keeps the repetition condition and body together.

quiz.prompt: The jump skips Work. Which line remains?
quiz.explanation: Execution resumes at the labeled End statement.

quiz.prompt: No jump occurs. How many labeled-path messages print?
quiz.explanation: Normal fall-through reaches B after A; the false if never jumps.

quiz.prompt: An error path sets a flag before jumping. Which status prints?
quiz.explanation: The assignment to nine is bypassed, leaving two.

quiz.prompt: If a second allocation fails, which earlier resource still needs release?
quiz.explanation: Failure of the later acquisition does not erase earlier ownership.

keyPoints.en: goto targets a label in the same function.
Labels do not replace structured loops for ordinary work.
keyPoints.bn: সাধারণ repetition-এ label-এর বদলে loop লেখো।

keyPoints.en: A shared cleanup path can release partially acquired resources.
keyPoints.bn: আংশিক resource পাওয়া গেলেও এক cleanup পথে ছাড়া যায়।

keyPoints.en: Initialize resource pointers before failure jumps.
keyPoints.bn: ব্যর্থতার jump-এর আগেই pointer শুরু করো।

keyPoints.en: Every owning exit path must perform cleanup.
keyPoints.bn: resource যার কাছে আছে, তার প্রতিটি exit পথে cleanup লাগবে।

examQuestions.question: Where must a goto target label belong?
examQuestions.answerHtml: In the same function. The jump cannot transfer between functions.

examQuestions.question: Can ordinary execution reach a label without goto?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. Labels mark statements and do not block fall-through.

End

Execution resumes at the labeled End statement.

examQuestions.question: Read fail_stage 0, 1 or 2. After Input: set acquired=1 after stage one succeeds and acquired=2 after stage two succeeds. Stage 1 or 2 fails when named by input; jump to cleanup then. Print Work only when neither fails. Always print Released=N with the number acquired, then newline.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int fail_stage;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d", &fail_stage) != 1 || fail_stage < 0 || fail_stage > 2) {
        return 1;
    }
    int acquired = 0;
    if (fail_stage == 1) {
        goto cleanup;
    }
    acquired = 1;
    if (fail_stage == 2) {
        goto cleanup;
    }
    acquired = 2;
    puts("Work");
    cleanup:
    printf("Released=%d\n", acquired);
    return 0;
}

This model exposes every partial-ownership path without relying on allocation failure.
